title: Customer query latency and telemetry contract for VPC & on‑prem
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary

This document defines the customer-facing query latency contract and the minimum telemetry/evidence requirements for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It is intended for SREs, delivery engineers, and customer security/compliance teams to: (a) set measurable latency SLOs by API type, (b) standardize telemetry schema and sampling policies that preserve customer privacy, and (c) describe an evidence bundle and verification process for audits and SLA disputes.

Scope

- Applies to all private deployment variants (VPC, on-prem appliance, and hybrid control-plane).
- Covers request-level latency SLOs for: text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Defines telemetry fields, retention/sampling defaults, and acceptable evidence package contents for customer and regulator reviews.
- Does NOT prescribe cloud vendor-specific logging backends; focuses on schema and guarantees.

Latency SLOs (per API flavor)

The SLOs below represent the default contract offered to customers. Individual contracts may override these but must be documented in the customer acceptance artifact.

| API flavor | SLO (P50) | SLO (P95) | SLO (P99) | Measurement window | Notes |
|------------|----------:|---------:|---------:|-------------------:|-------|
| Embeddings (single-vector) | 25 ms | 80 ms | 200 ms | 30d rolling | Measured end-to-end after tenant proxy; excludes model cold start > 10s |
| Text generation (short prompts, <=256 tokens) | 60 ms per token | 200 ms per token | 500 ms per token | 30d rolling | Token-level breakdown required when available |
| Chat (turn-based, KV cache present) | 50 ms | 180 ms | 450 ms | 30d rolling | Measure after tokenization; include cache hit ratio metric |
| Reranking (batch <= 32) | 150 ms | 500 ms | 1.5 s | 30d rolling | Batch size must be reported with latency metric |

Acceptable deviation margin: contracts may allow up to +20% P95 in first 72h of production (ramp) provided telemetry shows stable trend and corrective plan.

Telemetry contract (schema and requirements)

Minimum required fields (per-request):
- request_id (string, RFC4122 UUID recommended)
- tenant_id (string; opaque customer identifier assigned at provisioning)
- api_flavor (enum: embeddings|generation|chat|reranking)
- model_id (string; canonical model id and version)
- timestamp_received_utc (ISO8601)
- timestamp_response_sent_utc (ISO8601)
- latency_ms (integer; response_sent - received in ms)
- kv_cache_hit (enum: yes|no|unknown) — only for chat/generation
- batch_size (integer) — only for reranking/batched endpoints
- token_count_input (integer) and token_count_output (integer) — when available
- outcome_code (enum: success|fallback|error|throttled)
- error_code (string) — optional, only present if outcome_code != success
- sample_rate (float) — telemetry sampler should annotate actual sampling rate used for that tenant and time window

Additional optional telemetry:
- host_gpu_temperature_c (float)
- kernel_variant (string)
- quantization_profile (string)

Sampling, retention and privacy constraints

- Default sampling: 100% for P50/P95 SLO calculation during first 72 hours after cutover; thereafter default 5% tail-sampling with strong preference for including all latency > P95.
- Sampling must be biased toward high-latency events for SLA evidence: ensure capture of all samples above the tenant's P95 threshold during measurement windows.
- PII policy: prompts and raw outputs are considered customer-owned data. By default telemetry must not include raw prompt/output text. If customer requests prompt-level traces for debugging, an explicit consent and egress agreement must be in the customer contract and the data must be stored in a restricted encrypted bucket with audit logs.
- Retention defaults: 90 days for full per-request telemetry (restricted access), 365 days for aggregated SLO metrics (P50/P95/P99 per hour/day). Longer retention requires explicit procurement/contract.

Evidence bundle for audits and SLA disputes

When a customer requests an evidence package to substantiate an SLO breach or for regulatory audit, the minimal deliverable is:
1) Aggregated SLO time-series for the requested window (P50/P95/P99 per hour) in CSV or Parquet.
2) Per-request sampled records that show the breach window (matching schema fields above). Include at least 1,000 samples or all samples captured during the window, whichever is smaller.
3) Operator-run acceptance test results (synthetic traces) for the same model_id and deployment topology, with timestamps.
4) System-level annotations: ongoing maintenance events, autoscaler events, capacity pressure notes, and kernel-level known issues (if any) that impacted the window.
5) Chain of custody file: who pulled the data, when, filters applied, and a checksum of the bundle.

Evidence production SLA: Redwood will prepare the evidence bundle within 5 business days for standard requests. For regulated customers with 24/48h evidence SLA in their contract, escalate to the regional Field Delivery lead.

Acceptance criteria for new private deployments

- Pre-cutover: synthetic-run P95 must be within 110% of contract P95 for 24h continuous run.
- Post-cutover (first 72h): 100% sampling enabled and automated alert if observed P95 > contract threshold.
- Post-cutover (30d): rolling 30d measurement must meet contract SLOs or a remediation plan must be accepted by the customer.

Onboarding checklist (delivery and engineering)

1. Confirm tenant_id mapping and provisioning in site configuration.
2. Enable per-request telemetry schema on tenant's tenant_id and validate fields using local dry-run (see CLI example).
3. Run 24h synthetic workload that mirrors customer QPS and token profile. Capture baseline SLOs.
4. Agree sampling and retention policy with customer; capture consent artifact if raw prompt/output traces are requested.
5. Generate and sign the acceptance artifact (CSV of synthetic run + measured SLOs).

Operator playbook: diagnosing a reported latency breach (numbered steps)

1. Triage: Confirm the tenant, time-range, and API flavor from the customer report. Ask for request_id(s) if available.
2. Quick health check (5 minutes): check host GPU load, autoscaler events, and network interface metrics for the tenant-specific slices.
3. Fetch aggregated SLOs for the window (hourly P95). Compare against contract thresholds.
4. Pull per-request sampled telemetry for the affected window using the evidence pull CLI (example below). If sampling rate is low, increase sampling and re-run synthetic tests.
5. If traces show model-side latency (token-level), capture kernel_variant and quantization_profile from host logs.
6. Create an incident if P95 > contract threshold for > 3 consecutive hours or if customer-visible errors exceed 1% of requests.
7. Communicate with customer: share immediate mitigation steps (traffic shaping, routing to a fallback model, or temporary capacity reservation).

CLI examples and snippets

- Validate telemetry schema (operator host):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" \
    -X POST https://local-telemetry-collector/_validate \
    -d '{"tenant_id":"TENANT-UUID","sample_rate":0.05,"schema_check":true}'

- Pull evidence bundle (operator):
  redwoodctl evidence pull --tenant TENANT-UUID --from 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-08-02T00:00:00Z --fields request_id,tenant_id,api_flavor,model_id,latency_ms,outcome_code --out /tmp/evidence-bundle-20260801.tar.gz

Telemetry sample (per-request JSON snippet, redacted):
  {
    "request_id": "a3f5c2d8-6b9e-4b1d-8be5-0c1d2e3f4a5b",
    "tenant_id": "cust-001234",
    "api_flavor": "generation",
    "model_id": "open-codex-xl:v1.3.0",
    "timestamp_received_utc": "2026-08-01T12:34:56.789Z",
    "timestamp_response_sent_utc": "2026-08-01T12:34:57.045Z",
    "latency_ms": 256,
    "kv_cache_hit": "yes",
    "token_count_input": 32,
    "token_count_output": 48,
    "outcome_code": "success",
    "sample_rate": 0.05
  }

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: Private Deployments Delivery (eng-delivery) — contact: eng-delivery@redwood.ai
- SRE on-call: use the established oncall rotation; page if incident thresholds are met.
- Field Delivery and Customer Success must be looped for SLA disputes.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Within 2 business days: Delivery lead responds with preliminary analysis.
- Within 5 business days: Evidence bundle delivered and remediation plan proposed.
- Contractually-specified timelines supersede defaults.

Appendix: audit checklist and quick checks

- Verify presence of required fields in at least one sampled record for the window.
- Confirm sampling rate annotation in records equals expected rate documented for the tenant.
- Validate checksums of evidence bundle and append chain-of-custody metadata.
- If raw prompts/outputs were requested, ensure encrypted bucket path, KMS key id, and requestor consent file are included.

Related links
- Onboarding readiness checklist: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library/customer-onboarding-deployment-readiness-and-risk-checklist-2026
- Post-install telemetry guide: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/post-installation-telemetry-and-acceptance-checklist-2026

Glossary
- Pxx: percentile over the measurement window.
- tenant_id: internal opaque id for customer tenancy.
- evidence bundle: curated set of aggregated metrics, sampled traces, and operator notes for audits.
